title: Day 1: Set up your project skeleton
brief: Initialize your repo, folder structure, and README. A clean start makes day 60 easier than day 1.
tasks: Create a public GitHub repo for your track project
Add a README with your project's one-line pitch
Push your first commit

title: Day 2: Wireframe your core screen
brief: Sketch the single screen a user will see most. Paper, Figma, or the back of a notebook all count.
tasks: Sketch the main screen of your project
List the 3 actions a user can take on it
Save the wireframe to your repo as an image

title: Day 3: Build your first static layout
brief: Turn yesterday's wireframe into markup. No logic yet — just structure and spacing.
tasks: Build the HTML/JSX structure for your main screen
Style it with your framework of choice
Commit with message: 'day N: static layout'

title: Day 4: Wire up your data model
brief: Decide what a single 'item' in your app looks like, and write it down before you write code for it.
tasks: Define your core data shape (JSON or schema)
Create 3 sample records
Render them as a static list

title: Day 5: Add your first interaction
brief: Pick one button. Make it do something real — not just log to console.
tasks: Implement one working click or tap interaction
Handle the empty/loading state for it
Commit and note what broke along the way

title: Day 6: Style pass: make it look intentional
brief: Nothing kills momentum like an ugly build. Give today fully to visual polish.
tasks: Pick a 3-color palette and apply it consistently
Fix spacing on your smallest screen size
Screenshot before/after for your notes

title: Day 7: Handle your first edge case
brief: Every real app breaks somewhere. Find one place yours does, and fix it.
tasks: Identify one input that currently breaks your UI
Add a guard or fallback for it
Write a one-line comment explaining the fix

title: Day 8: Connect to mock or live data
brief: Move from hardcoded arrays to something that resembles a real data source.
tasks: Move your sample data into a separate JSON file
Fetch or import it instead of hardcoding in components
Confirm the UI still renders correctly

title: Day 9: Add navigation between two screens
brief: An app is more than one screen. Build the second one today.
tasks: Create a second route or screen
Add a way to move between the two
Test both directions of navigation

title: Day 10: Write your first real form
brief: Forms are where most learning apps fall apart. Build one that actually validates input.
tasks: Build a form with at least 2 fields
Add basic validation (required, format)
Show a clear error state

title: Day 11: Refactor without changing behavior
brief: Today, don't add anything. Make what exists easier to read.
tasks: Rename one unclear variable or component
Split one oversized file into two
Confirm nothing broke after the refactor

title: Day 12: Add a loading and empty state
brief: Design for the moment before there's data, not just the moment after.
tasks: Add a loading indicator for at least one view
Add an empty-state message for when there's no data
Compare how both feel on a 390px screen

title: Day 13: Document what you built this week
brief: Future-you (and recruiters) will thank present-you for writing this down.
tasks: Update your README with what's working so far
List 2 things you'd do differently
Push the updated docs

title: Day 14: Ship a small but real feature
brief: Pick the smallest genuinely useful feature you haven't built yet, and ship only that.
tasks: Choose one feature you can finish today
Build and test it end to end
Keep the commit scoped to just this feature

title: Day 15: Improve your mobile layout
brief: Most of your users are on a phone, late at night. Design for that reality today.
tasks: Test your app at 390px width
Fix any text truncation or overflow
Check tap target sizes are comfortable

title: Day 16: Add error handling to one flow
brief: Pick your riskiest flow — the one most likely to fail — and make failure survivable.
tasks: Identify your most fragile user flow
Add a try/catch or fallback UI for it
Write down what a user sees when it fails

title: Day 17: Write a test for your riskiest function
brief: You don't need full coverage. You need confidence in the part that scares you most.
tasks: Pick the function you trust least
Write one test for its main behavior
Run it and confirm it passes

title: Day 18: Polish your onboarding moment
brief: The first 10 seconds decide whether someone stays. Give them your full attention today.
tasks: Review what a brand-new user sees first
Cut anything that doesn't help them get started
Add one line of guidance if it's missing

title: Day 19: Add a share or export feature
brief: Give your project a way to leave the app — a link, an image, a download.
tasks: Pick one artifact worth sharing (result, score, output)
Build a simple share or export action for it
Test that the shared output makes sense out of context

title: Day 20: Mid-challenge review
brief: Step back. Look at day 1's commit next to today's. Note the distance.
tasks: Re-read your day 1 README
List 3 things that changed since then
Post a short reflection alongside today's proof
